bull.b: Sustained revenue expansion alongside a growing managed and planned capacity base indicates increasing customer demand for Soluna’s renewable-powered compute infrastructure. If execution continues, this platform expansion can support broader hosting and AI revenue over the next several quarters.

Debt reduction and stronger liquidity improve Soluna’s financial flexibility as it funds construction and development activity. A less leveraged balance sheet can reduce interest burden, release project liens, and provide greater capacity to pursue AI infrastructure opportunities.

Preserved interconnection capacity is a meaningful infrastructure advantage in a crowded Texas large-load queue. It supports the company’s ability to convert renewable power into computing capacity and provides a firmer foundation for its multi-gigawatt AI and HPC development pipeline.

bear.b: Revenue growth is not currently translating into sustainable earnings, because near-breakeven gross margins and substantial net losses absorb the benefits of scale. Persistent operating losses weaken internally funded expansion and make future profitability dependent on major execution improvement.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the existing business is not self-funding its operations or development program. Continued cash consumption can increase reliance on external capital, constrain project pacing, and reduce resilience if financing conditions remain difficult.

Major AI growth plans still depend on converting preliminary commercial arrangements into signed leases and completing related project agreements. Delays could defer revenue and financing, while tighter debt markets and higher borrowing costs may make planned project structures harder to execute.
